questions.question: The Indian telecom sector was liberalised under which year’s Telecom Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1994**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian telecom sector was liberalized under the **National Telecom Policy of 1994**.
 
• The policy introduced **private sector participation** in providing telecom services, which was earlier monopolized by the government.
 
• It aimed to **increase tele-density** and improve the quality of services by allowing private players to operate in the telecom space.
 
• The 1994 policy laid the groundwork for further liberalization and reforms, including the entry of private companies in the telecom sector.
 
• This reform was a major step towards **modernizing India's telecom infrastructure** and ensuring widespread connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI):** Established in 1997, TRAI is responsible for regulating telecom services, including tariffs and ensuring fair competition.
 
• **Subsequent Policies:** The 1999 New Telecom Policy (NTP) further liberalized the sector and introduced revenue-sharing models instead of fixed license fees.
 
• **Telecom Revolution:** The liberalization and reforms of the 1990s paved the way for the telecom revolution in India, with rapid growth in mobile phone penetration and internet services.
 
• **FDI in Telecom:** The sector has also attracted significant foreign direct investment (FDI), with the government allowing up to 100% FDI in certain areas.
 
• **Impact:** Today, India is one of the largest telecom markets globally, with billions of subscribers and a robust digital infrastructure.

questions.question: In South Indian temple architecture, what is the name of the stepped or pyramidal structure built above the sanctum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vimana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In South Indian temple architecture, the term **Vimana** refers to the **pyramidal or stepped structure** built directly above the sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• The Vimana is often elaborately decorated with intricate carvings, sculptures, and ornamental details, showcasing the artistic skill of ancient Indian craftsmen.
 
• This feature is a distinguishing aspect of Dravidian temple architecture, commonly seen in temples of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The Vimana serves not only as an architectural feature but also as a symbolic representation of the sacred Mount Meru, believed to be the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
• Famous examples of Vimanas can be seen in temples like the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Thanjavur and the **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai.
 
• [IMAGE: https://www.mahabalipuram.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Side_profile_Brihadeeswara-1024x768.jpeg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adhisthana:**

 
 
• The Adhisthana is the base or platform on which the temple structure is built. It provides stability and often contains ornamental moldings.
 
 
 
• **Jagati:**
 
 
• The Jagati refers to a raised platform that surrounds the temple, often used for circumambulation (pradakshina) by devotees.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa:**
 
 
• A Mandapa is a pillared hall or pavilion in a temple, used for congregational purposes, rituals, and ceremonies. It is often located in front of the sanctum.
 
 
 
• **South Indian Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• South Indian temples are primarily built in the Dravidian architectural style, characterized by towering gopurams (gateway towers), Vimanas, and intricate carvings.
 
• The temple layout often includes key components like the Garbhagriha (sanctum), Vimana, Mandapa, and Prakara (enclosure walls).

questions.question: The popular folk dance of Bihar, which represents the love and quarrel of a married couple, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jat-Jatin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jat-Jatin** is a popular folk dance of Bihar, often performed during the monsoon season.
 
• The dance is a symbolic representation of the **love and quarrels of a married couple**, portraying their emotional dynamics.
 
• It is widely performed in the Mithila region of Bihar and adjoining areas, showcasing the cultural richness of the state.
 
• The dance is accompanied by traditional folk songs that narrate the stories of **Jat (husband) and Jatin (wife)**.
 
• Jat-Jatin serves as a form of entertainment and a medium for expressing the daily lives and struggles of rural communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folk Dances of Bihar:**

 
 
• Some other famous folk dances of Bihar include **Sohar-Khilouna, Bidesia, Jhijhiya, and Kajari.**
 
• These dances are deeply rooted in the traditions and practices of rural Bihar, celebrating various aspects of life.
 
 
 
• **Mithila Region:**
 
 
• The Mithila region is known for its unique cultural heritage, including **folk art, music, and dance**.
 
• It is also famous for the world-renowned **Madhubani paintings**.
 
 
 
• **Music in Jat-Jatin:**
 
 
• The music accompanying the Jat-Jatin dance typically uses traditional instruments such as **dholak, harmonium, and manjira**.
 
• The lyrics focus on themes of rural life, love, and hardships faced by couples.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Jat-Jatin reflects the social and emotional aspects of relationships in rural Bihar.
 
• It provides insights into the challenges faced by couples due to migration, poverty, and societal norms.

questions.question: Saura painting, a tribal art form, is traditionally practiced by communities in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saura painting is a tribal art form originating from the Saura tribe of Odisha, India.
 
• These paintings are traditionally created on walls of houses and depict daily life, religious practices, and nature.
 
• Saura art uses natural colors derived from soil, leaves, and rice paste, making it eco-friendly and sustainable.
 
• The paintings are characterized by geometric patterns and intricate detailing, often resembling Warli art but with distinct motifs.
 
• Saura art holds cultural and spiritual significance as it is used to invoke blessings and depict tribal folklore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saura Tribe:**

 
 
• The Saura tribe is one of the oldest tribes in Odisha and is known for its rich cultural heritage and traditional practices.
 
• They primarily inhabit the districts of Ganjam, Rayagada, and Koraput in Odisha.
 
• The tribe follows its own distinct language and customs, contributing to the diversity of Indian tribal culture.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Techniques:**
 
 
• Saura paintings are created using freehand drawing without pre-sketching, showcasing the skill of the artist.
 
• Figures in the paintings are stylized and feature stick-like human and animal forms.
 
• The themes often revolve around nature, hunting, rituals, and community activities.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Warli Art:**
 
 
• Saura art and Warli art are often confused due to similar geometric patterns.
 
• Unlike Warli, Saura art focuses more on religious and spiritual themes.
 
• Saura paintings include intricate borders and are more densely populated with motifs.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve and promote Saura art through exhibitions and workshops.
 
• Government initiatives in Odisha encourage tribal artisans to sustain this traditional art form.
 
• Saura art has gained international recognition for its aesthetic appeal and cultural significance.

questions.question: Which ruler regained his lost kingdom by 1555 after defeating Sher Shah Suri's successors, thereby marking the end of the Second Afghan Empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Humayun**, the second Mughal emperor, regained his lost kingdom after defeating the successors of **Sher Shah Suri** in **1555**.
 
• He recaptured Delhi and Agra from the Afghan rulers, marking the end of the **Second Afghan Empire**.
 
• Humayun's return to power was aided by strategic alliances, including support from the Persian ruler Shah Tahmasp.
 
• His victory restored the Mughal Empire's presence in India, laying the foundation for the reign of his son, Akbar the Great.
 
• Humayun's return to the throne was short-lived, as he passed away in 1556, shortly after regaining power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Afghan Empire:**

 
 
• It was established by Sher Shah Suri, who overthrew Humayun in 1540 and ruled until his death in 1545.
 
• Sher Shah's successors were unable to maintain control, leading to Humayun's return.
 
 
 
• **Shah Tahmasp's Support:**
 
 
• Humayun sought refuge in Persia after losing his kingdom and received military assistance from Shah Tahmasp.
 
• This alliance was pivotal in Humayun's successful campaign against the Afghan rulers.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire:**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire was one of the largest and most influential empires in Indian history, known for its cultural and architectural contributions.
 
• Humayun's restoration strengthened the Mughal dynasty, which reached its zenith under Akbar.
 
 
 
• **Humayun's Tomb:**
 
 
• Built by Humayun's widow, **Bega Begum**, it is one of the first examples of Mughal architecture in India.
 
• Located in Delhi, it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **and inspired later architectural marvels like the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Which ruler, upon his death in 1530, left behind a newly established empire that stretched across northern India—from the Indus River in the west to Bihar in the east, and from the Himalayas in the north to Gwalior in the south?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Babur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, died in **1530**, leaving behind a vast empire.
 
• The empire stretched across northern India—from the **Indus River in the west** to **Bihar in the east**, and from the **Himalayas in the north** to **Gwalior in the south**.
 
• Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)**, which marked the establishment of the Mughal Empire.
 
• He was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and Genghis Khan on his mother's side, which gave legitimacy to his rule.
 
• Babur's autobiography, **"Baburnama,"** provides detailed accounts of his life, campaigns, and the socio-political conditions of his time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Empire:**

 
 
• The Mughal Empire ruled most of India and Pakistan from the early 16th to the mid-18th century.
 
• It is known for its significant contributions to art, architecture, culture, and centralized governance.
 
• Notable Mughal rulers include Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb.
 
 
 
• **Babur's military tactics:**
 
 
• Babur introduced **modern artillery and gunpowder** to Indian warfare during his campaigns.
 
• He employed the **"Tulughma" strategy**, dividing his army into flanking, center, and reserve units for better maneuverability.
 
 
 
• **Baburnama:**
 
 
• Babur wrote his autobiography, "Baburnama," in Chagatai Turkish, which was later translated into Persian.
 
• The book provides insights into Babur's thoughts, personal life, and the cultural landscape of his era.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• Fought in 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi.
 
• This battle marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of Mughal rule in India.

questions.question: Which princely ruler patronised the Sikh community and institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhupinder Singh of Patiala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala** was a notable patron of the **Sikh community **and played a key role in preserving Sikh religious and cultural heritage.
 
• He contributed significantly to the construction and renovation of Sikh religious shrines, including the **Golden Temple in Amritsar**.
 
• The Maharaja supported Sikh institutions, including funding for educational initiatives and religious activities to promote Sikhism.
 
• He was a key figure in the Sikh community during the early 20th century and maintained close ties with the **Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee** (SGPC).
 
• Maharaja Bhupinder Singh is also remembered for his efforts to preserve Sikh traditions and for promoting unity within the Sikh community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib):**

 
 
• The Golden Temple, located in Amritsar, Punjab, is the holiest shrine in Sikhism.
 
• It was **founded by the fourth Sikh Guru, Guru Ram Das**, and later completed by **Guru Arjan Dev**.
 
• The temple represents Sikh values of equality, unity, and service to humanity.
 
 
 
• **Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC):**
 
 
• The SGPC is an organization responsible for managing Sikh gurdwaras and promoting Sikh religious activities.
 
• It plays a vital role in preserving Sikh history, culture, and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Princely States of India:**
 
 
• During British rule, princely states were semi-autonomous regions governed by local monarchs under British suzerainty.
 
• Patiala was one of the largest princely states in Punjab.
 
 
 
• **Bhupinder Singh's Legacy:**
 
 
• Apart from his contributions to Sikhism, Maharaja Bhupinder Singh is also remembered for his progressive reforms in Patiala, including modern infrastructure and military advancements.
 
• He was an influential leader and diplomat, representing India in international arenas, such as the League of Nations.

questions.question: What popular title is used to refer to the Bengali poet Jibanananda Das?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rupashi Banglar Kabi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jibanananda Das, a renowned Bengali poet, is often referred to as **Rupashi Banglar Kabi** (Poet of Beautiful Bengal).
 
• This title is attributed to him due to his poetic works that vividly depict the natural beauty and essence of Bengal.
 
• His famous anthology "**Rupasi Bangla**" is considered a masterpiece that captures the rural landscapes and culture of Bengal.
 
• Jibanananda Das is regarded as one of the greatest modern poets in Bengali literature, often celebrated for his unique style and profound imagery.
 
• His works reflect themes of nostalgia, longing, and a deep connection to the land and heritage of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jibanananda Das's Literary Contributions**

 
 
• He introduced modernist themes and styles in Bengali poetry, breaking away from traditional structures.
 
• Some of his notable works include "**Banalata Sen**", "**Rupasi Bangla**", and "**Dhusar Pandulipi**".
 
• His poetry is characterized by vivid imagery, metaphors, and a melancholic tone.
 
 
 
• **Rupasi Bangla**
 
 
• "Rupasi Bangla" is a collection of poems written by Jibanananda Das, celebrating the beauty of rural Bengal.
 
• It was published posthumously in 1957, though the poems were written much earlier.
 
• The anthology is widely appreciated for its lyrical quality and portrayal of Bengal's landscapes.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Jibanananda Das**
 
 
• Jibanananda Das remains a significant figure in Bengali literature, influencing generations of poets and writers.
 
• He is often referred to as the "silent revolutionary" for his unique contribution to modern Bengali poetry.
 
• His works have been translated into several languages, earning him global recognition.
 
 
 
• **Modern Bengali Poetry**
 
 
• The modernist movement in Bengali poetry emerged in the early 20th century, with poets like Jibanananda Das leading the charge.
 
• It focused on introspection, individualism, and breaking away from traditional themes.
 
• Jibanananda Das's poetry is a cornerstone of this movement, blending aesthetic beauty with philosophical depth.

questions.question: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs), the Government of India's education initiatives for tribal communities, were introduced in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997-98**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs)** were introduced by the Government of India in the year **1997-98** to provide quality education to tribal students.
 
• The scheme was launched under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to ensure access to education for Scheduled Tribe (ST) students in remote areas.
 
• EMRSs aim to provide holistic education from Class VI to XII, with an emphasis on both academic and extracurricular activities.
 
• Each school is equipped to accommodate 480 students, providing free education, boarding, and lodging facilities to the students.
 
• The government has set a target of establishing one EMRS in every block with a significant tribal population (at least 50% ST population and 20,000 tribal people).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objective of EMRSs:**

 
 
• To promote the educational advancement of Scheduled Tribe (ST) children by providing quality education in a residential setup.
 
• To enable students to access opportunities in higher education and employment.
 
 
 
• **Salient Features of EMRSs:**
 
 
• Schools are set up with modern infrastructure, including hostels, libraries, and sports facilities.
 
• Focus on preserving tribal culture and heritage alongside mainstream education.
 
• Students are provided free uniforms, textbooks, and stationery.
 
 
 
• **Expansion Goals:**
 
 
• By 2025, the government aims to establish 740 EMRSs across the country to cater to tribal students.
 
• This will ensure a greater reach and reduce educational inequalities for tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Associated Schemes:**
 
 
• EMRSs are a part of the government's larger initiative to support tribal development, alongside schemes like the Tribal Sub-Plan and Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana.
 
• Additional scholarships and support programs are also provided to students to promote higher education.

questions.question: Under the Bharatmala Pariyojana, how many kilometres of roads are slated for development to improve border and international connectivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2,000 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the **Bharatmala Pariyojana**, the Government of India aims to develop **2,000 km of roads** to enhance border and international connectivity.
 
• The Bharatmala Pariyojana is a **central government initiative** for road infrastructure development across India.
 
• This scheme focuses on **optimizing freight movement, improving connectivity**, and developing economic corridors, inter-corridors, and feeder routes.
 
• The program is expected to strengthen India's strategic borders and foster better connectivity with neighboring countries.
 
• The Bharatmala Pariyojana is implemented by the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways** (MoRTH).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana**

 
 
• Bharatmala Pariyojana is India's largest road development initiative aimed at improving **national highways and infrastructure.**
 
• It focuses on **connecting rural areas, border regions, and economically backward regions** to mainstream development.
 
• This ambitious scheme covers **economic corridors, feeder roads, coastal and port connectivity roads, and greenfield expressways.**
 
• It seeks to enhance India’s trade potential by improving connectivity to major ports and trade hubs.
 
 
 
• **Border Connectivity under Bharatmala**
 
 
• The program prioritizes road infrastructure development in **strategic border areas**, ensuring better accessibility for defense and trade purposes.
 
• Improved border roads facilitate movement of goods and military personnel to remote and sensitive regions.
 
• This initiative strengthens India's **international relations** by ensuring smoother cross-border trade and connectivity.
 
 
 
• **Funding and Implementation**
 
 
• The Bharatmala Pariyojana is a **centrally-funded scheme** with significant budget allocation and private sector participation.
 
• The project is implemented in phases to ensure effective utilization of resources and timely completion.
 
• The total cost for the scheme is estimated to be approximately **₹5.35 lakh crore.**
 
 
 
• **Impact on Economy**
 
 
• The development of roads under Bharatmala Pariyojana is expected to **reduce logistics costs** and improve efficiency in freight transportation.
 
• It will contribute to **economic growth** by fostering trade, tourism, and industry in remote and underdeveloped areas.

questions.question: In Gond painting, what is the traditional name given to the handmade brush used by artists locally?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Koochi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Koochi** is the traditional name given to the **handmade brush used by Gond artists** for painting.
 
• It is typically handcrafted using natural materials such as bamboo or wood for the handle and locally available hair or fibers for the bristles.
 
• Koochi brushes are used to create** intricate patterns and fine details**, which are characteristic of Gond art.
 
• Gond artists rely heavily on these traditional tools to maintain the authenticity and cultural essence of their artwork.
 
• This handmade brush is an integral part of the Gond painting tradition, reflecting the deep connection between the art and its cultural roots.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gond Painting:**

 
 
• Gond painting is a form of tribal art practiced by the Gond community, one of the largest indigenous groups in India.
 
• The art form is characterized by intricate patterns, bright colors, and themes inspired by nature, folklore, and daily life.
 
• Traditionally, Gond paintings were created on walls and floors during festivals and rituals.
 
• Modern Gond art has gained international recognition and is now done on canvases, paper, and fabrics.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tools in Tribal Art:**
 
 
• Traditional tools like Koochi play a crucial role in preserving the authenticity of tribal art forms.
 
• They are often made using eco-friendly and locally sourced materials, reflecting the sustainable practices of indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Other Traditional Art Materials:**
 
 
• Natural dyes derived from plants, minerals, and soil are used in Gond painting.
 
• The colors used in Gond art are vibrant and often symbolize different emotions and elements of nature.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Gond Art:**
 
 
• Gond art has been showcased in museums and galleries around the world, bringing attention to India's rich tribal heritage.
 
• Prominent Gond artists like Jangarh Singh Shyam have played a significant role in popularizing this art form globally.

questions.question: The Desert National Park is renowned for which endangered bird species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Indian Bustard**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Indian Bustard is critically endangered and is one of the heaviest flying birds, found mainly in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The Desert National Park in Rajasthan is one of the primary habitats for the Great Indian Bustard, offering protection to this species.
 
• Its population has drastically declined due to habitat loss, poaching, and human-induced activities, leading to its inclusion in the IUCN Red List under the "Critically Endangered" category.
 
• The Great Indian Bustard is a ground-nesting bird, primarily dependent on grasslands and arid regions for survival.
 
• Conservation programs such as captive breeding and habitat restoration are being actively pursued by the Indian government and wildlife organizations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Desert National Park**

 
 
• Located in Rajasthan, it is one of the largest national parks in India, covering an area of 3162 km².
 
• The park's ecosystem includes sand dunes, rocky terrain, and sparse vegetation, ideal for desert wildlife.
 
• Besides the Great Indian Bustard, the park is home to other species such as Indian fox, desert cat, and sandgrouse.
 
 
 
• **Great Indian Bustard Conservation**
 
 
• The government has launched Project Great Indian Bustard to protect and conserve this critically endangered species.
 
• The Bustard Recovery Program involves captive breeding efforts and habitat management.
 
• Artificial egg incubation and predator control measures are also being implemented to ensure population growth.
 
 
 
• **Critically Endangered Species**
 
 
• Species classified as "Critically Endangered" under the IUCN Red List are at the highest risk of extinction in the wild.
 
• Global efforts such as habitat preservation, anti-poaching laws, and community involvement are vital for their survival.
 
 
 
• **Grassland Ecosystems**
 
 
• Grasslands are crucial for the survival of many species like the Great Indian Bustard, providing food and nesting habitats.
 
• Human activities, including agriculture and urbanization, have severely impacted grassland ecosystems.
 
• Restoring grasslands is essential for maintaining biodiversity and ecological balance.

questions.question: When was the protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife as a directive added in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife were added as **Directive Principles of State Policy** under Article 48A of the Indian Constitution in **1976**.
 
• This amendment was made through the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, which is considered one of the most extensive amendments in Indian constitutional history.
 
• Article 48A directs the State to endeavor to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country.
 
• Additionally, Article 51A(g) was also added through the 42nd Amendment, which makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act was enacted during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, who emphasized environmental protection as a key priority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are guidelines for the central and state governments to ensure social and economic welfare in India.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, but they are fundamental in governance.
 
• Environmental protection was incorporated under DPSPs through Article 48A, emphasizing sustainable development.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act of 1976:**
 
 
• It introduced significant changes to the Constitution, including adding new directives and duties.
 
• It added Articles 48A and 51A(g), focusing on environmental conservation.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its sweeping impact on constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution through the 42nd Amendment under Article 51A.
 
• Article 51A(g) specifically states that citizens must protect and improve the environment.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-enforceable but serve as moral obligations for Indian citizens.
 
 
 
• **Global Environmental Awareness:**
 
 
• The incorporation of environmental protection in the Indian Constitution was influenced by global movements like the **United Nations Conference on the Human Environment (1972)** held in Stockholm.
 
• India was one of the signatories to the Stockholm Declaration, which emphasized environmental conservation worldwide.

questions.question: When were privy purses officially abolished in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1971**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Privy purses were annual payments made to the rulers of erstwhile princely states as part of the integration of these states into the Indian Union post-independence.
 
• These payments were guaranteed under Articles 291 and 362 of the Indian Constitution to ensure the cooperation of princely states during the process of integration.
 
• In 1971, under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, the 26th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted, officially abolishing privy purses.
 
• The 26th Amendment removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution and abolished the recognition of rulers as well as their privileges.
 
• The move was part of the broader effort to promote equality and eliminate the remnants of feudalism in independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privy Purses:**

 
 
• Privy purses were monetary allowances given to the rulers of princely states as part of their agreement to join India.
 
• The amount varied based on the size, revenue, and status of the princely state.
 
 
 
• **26th Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• This amendment was passed in 1971 and removed Articles 291 and 362 from the Indian Constitution.
 
• It ended the recognition of princely states and abolished all privileges, titles, and privy purses associated with them.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition of privy purses was seen as a step toward reducing inequality and strengthening the democratic fabric of India.
 
• It also marked the end of any feudal privileges and ensured that all citizens were treated equally under the law.
 
 
 
• **Integration of Princely States:**
 
 
• Post-independence, there were more than 550 princely states in India.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon played key roles in integrating these states into the Indian Union through diplomacy and negotiation.

questions.question: What is the main goal of the PM Gati Shakti initiative?
questions.solution:

• The initiative was launched on **October 13, 2021** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• It aims to bring 16 key ministries, including Railways and Roadways, together on a single platform to ensure **integrated planning and coordination for infrastructure projects**.
 
• The primary goal is to **reduce logistics costs, improve supply chain efficiency, and boost economic growth** through synchronized execution of infrastructure projects.
 
• It emphasizes the use of advanced technology such as GIS-based systems and satellite imagery to streamline planning and implementation processes.

• **Logistics cost in India:** High logistics costs in India (13-14% of GDP) have been a major hurdle to economic growth, and PM Gati Shakti aims to reduce these costs significantly.
 
• **GIS-based planning:** Geographic Information System (GIS) technology is used to visualize, analyze, and integrate data for precise infrastructure planning under the initiative.
 
• **Infrastructure boost:** The program is aligned with India's goal of becoming a $5 trillion economy by enhancing infrastructure and supply chain capabilities.
 
• **Economic benefits:** By improving connectivity and logistics, the initiative aims to attract investments, create jobs, and ensure faster movement of goods across the country.

questions.question: Jharkhand authorities have successfully relocated Jaigir, the first village inside the _________, entirely outside its core area.

• Palamu Tiger Reserve is located in the Latehar district of Jharkhand and was one of the first nine tiger reserves declared under Project Tiger in 1973.
 
• The relocation of Jaigir village is part of efforts to reduce human-wildlife conflict and ensure conservation of the core area of the reserve.
 
• Jaigir is the first village within the core area of Palamu Tiger Reserve that has been successfully relocated to minimize anthropogenic pressures on wildlife habitats.
 
• The process of relocation involved financial compensation and support to villagers for rehabilitation outside the reserve's core area.
 
• The initiative aligns with the National Tiger Conservation Authority's (NTCA) guidelines for sustainable conservation practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Project Tiger is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
• It covers 53 tiger reserves across India as of 2023.
 
 
 
• **Core and Buffer Zones:**
 
 
• Tiger reserves are divided into core and buffer zones for effective management.
 
• The core zone is strictly protected for wildlife conservation, while the buffer zone accommodates regulated human activities.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• NTCA was established in 2005 to strengthen tiger conservation efforts in India.
 
• It oversees the implementation of Project Tiger and ensures compliance with wildlife protection laws.
 
 
 
• **Human-Wildlife Conflict:**

• **Boliyan:**

questions.question: In which of the following dance forms vocal music is not used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a traditional Indian dance form primarily performed in the states of **Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand**.
 
• Unlike many other classical Indian dance forms, Chhau does not use **vocal music** during performances.
 
• The music accompanying Chhau performances is primarily instrumental and consists of traditional Indian instruments such as **dhol, dhamsa, and shehnai**.
 
• Chhau is characterized by its **martial movements**, masks (in certain variants), and themes often derived from Indian mythology.
 
• This dance form is known for its vigorous and dramatic movements, making it distinct from other Indian classical dances like Bharatanatyam, Kathak, and Odissi which incorporate vocal music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam heavily incorporates vocal music alongside instrumental music.
 
• The themes often revolve around **spiritual ideas, stories from Hindu mythology, and devotional content**.
 
• It uses intricate hand gestures (mudras) and facial expressions to narrate stories.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Originating from Odisha, Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India.
 
• It is performed to both **vocal and instrumental music**, often based on compositions of Jayadeva's "Gita Govinda."
 
• Odissi emphasizes fluid movements and tribhangi (three-bend posture).
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• A classical dance form from northern India, Kathak incorporates **vocal music and instrumental tabla and sitar performances**.
 
• The dance form is characterized by intricate footwork and spins.
 
• Its themes often include storytelling from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Indian Instruments in Dance Forms**
 
 
• **Dhol:** A percussion instrument used in Chhau performances.
 
• **Shehnai:** A wind instrument that provides melody in many Indian traditional performances.
 
• **Tabla:** A pair of drums often used in classical Indian music.

questions.question: In Warli painting, which natural material is used in the first step called 'Lipane' to prepare the wall?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Geru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geru** is a natural red ochre pigment used in **Warli painting**, particularly in the initial step known as 'Lipane'.
 
• 'Lipane' refers to the process of preparing the wall surface for painting by applying a smooth layer of geru mixed with water or cow dung.
 
• The use of geru gives the wall a distinctive **reddish-brown** or earthy tone, which serves as the base for the white rice paste designs in Warli art.
 
• This natural pigment is widely available and eco-friendly, aligning with the Warli tribe's connection to nature and sustainability.
 
• Geru creates a textured surface that enhances the **contrast** of the white rice paste used for drawing intricate patterns and motifs.
 
• The Warli paintings are deeply rooted in the tradition of the **Warli tribe**, predominantly found in the **North Sahyadri Range** of Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• The use of geru in 'Lipane' highlights the Warli tribe's reliance on **locally sourced materials** and their harmonious relationship with the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Rice Paste**__

 __
 
• **Rice paste** is indeed used in Warli painting but serves a different function. It is the primary medium for creating the iconic white motifs and patterns on the prepared red-brown surface.
 
• It is made by grinding rice into a fine paste, often mixed with water or a binding agent, to achieve a smooth consistency.
 
• The white rice paste symbolizes **purity** and is used to depict themes of life, nature, and cultural rituals.
 
 
 
• ** Sand**__
 __
 
• **Sand** is not a material typically associated with preparing the wall surface in Warli painting. However, sand may sometimes be mixed with materials like cow dung to create a rough surface for other traditional art forms.
 
• Sand lacks the distinct color and texture provided by geru, which is essential for the aesthetic appeal of Warli art.
 
 
 
• ** Charcoal**__
 
 
• **Charcoal** is a black pigment used in various art forms but is not a component of Warli painting.
 
• While charcoal could be used for sketching or other forms of tribal art, it does not serve the purpose of preparing the wall or creating motifs in Warli art.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT contribute much to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Increased plantation of native trees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increased plantation of native trees** is a sustainable practice and contributes to the **restoration** of the ecosystem.
 
• Native trees are well-adapted to the **climatic conditions** and soil types of the region, making them ideal for conserving the **local biodiversity.**
 
• Planting native species enhances the ability of the Thar Desert to combat **desertification**, as these trees can provide shade, prevent soil erosion, and improve soil moisture retention.
 
• These trees support the local **wildlife** by providing habitats and food sources, and they also preserve the ecosystem's **natural balance.**
 
• Unlike invasive species, native trees do not disrupt the existing ecological processes. Instead, they contribute to the **stability** and resilience of the environment.
 
• Efforts to plant native trees are often part of **governmental and non-governmental programs** aimed at combating desertification under initiatives such as the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).**
 
• This practice does not lead to any significant degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem but rather helps in its **long-term sustainability.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Grazing by livestock**__

 __
 
• **Grazing by livestock** is a major contributor to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem. Overgrazing leads to **soil erosion** and the destruction of vegetation, which are critical to maintaining the desert’s delicate ecological balance.
 
• Livestock grazing often reduces the availability of **native vegetation**, leading to the loss of habitat for local wildlife.
 
• Excessive grazing also disrupts the soil’s capacity to retain moisture, further exacerbating **desertification.**
 
 
 
• **Erratic rainfall**__
 __
 
• **Erratic rainfall** is another factor impacting the Thar Desert ecosystem. The desert region experiences highly unpredictable and irregular rainfall patterns, which affect the **growth of vegetation** and the availability of water resources.
 
• Sudden bursts of rainfall can lead to **soil erosion**, while prolonged drought periods can decrease the survival rate of plants and animals.
 
• This variability in precipitation is a natural characteristic of desert climates but becomes more pronounced with **climate change.**
 
 
 
• **Climate change**__
 
 
• **Climate change** has a profound impact on the Thar Desert ecosystem, as rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns intensify **desertification.**
 
• It leads to increased occurrences of **extreme weather events**, such as heatwaves and heavy storms, which disrupt the ecological balance.
 
• Climate change also affects the survival of **native flora and fauna**, as they struggle to adapt to the rapidly changing conditions.
 
• Global efforts to mitigate climate change, such as the **Paris Agreement**, aim to address these challenges to ecosystems worldwide, including the Thar Desert.

questions.question: In which of the following cities Gharanas of Thumri are based?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Banaras and Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thumri** is a semi-classical form of Indian vocal music known for its **expressive and romantic themes.**
 
• The two prominent **Gharanas** associated with Thumri are based in **Banaras** and **Lucknow**.
 
• **Banaras Gharana:** Known for its **spiritual and devotional touch,** this style emphasizes the lyrical aspect of Thumri with intricate melodic variations. It is often performed in a more relaxed and meditative manner.
 
• **Lucknow Gharana:** This Gharana is recognized for its **expressive and dramatic style**, focusing on the emotional depth and beauty of Thumri. It heavily incorporates gestures and facial expressions to convey the mood of the song.
 
• Both Gharanas have contributed significantly to the evolution and popularity of Thumri, making them integral to Indian classical music.
 
• Thumri is often accompanied by instruments such as the **tabla, harmonium, and sarangi**, enhancing its melodious appeal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agra and Kirana**__

 __
 
• The **Agra Gharana** is primarily known for its **Dhrupad and Khayal styles** rather than Thumri. It emphasizes robust and powerful singing techniques.
 
• The **Kirana Gharana** is famous for its focus on the **melodic and subtle nuances** of Khayal singing. It is not predominantly associated with Thumri.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior and Bhopal**__
 __
 
• The **Gwalior Gharana** is the **oldest Gharana** in Indian classical music, known for its Khayal style. It does not hold a significant tradition of Thumri singing.
 
• **Bhopal** does not have a notable Gharana associated with Thumri or any prominent style of Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Patiala and Talwandi**__
 
 
• The **Patiala Gharana** is renowned for its **Khayal and Tappa styles**, characterized by intricate rhythmic patterns and fast-paced singing.
 
• **Talwandi** Gharana is primarily associated with **Dhrupad style** and does not have a significant tradition of Thumri singing.
